rows.description: A teenager after hours of study or many decisions grabs whatever is easy, such as junk snacks or a quick reply. Choosing depletes mental energy.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student after a day of decisions about food, classes and plans defaults to impulse or avoidance in the evening.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A wise professional makes big decisions early in the day, uses routines for small ones, and avoids important choices when hungry, rushed or worn out.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young child in a toy shop with many choices freezes, cries or grabs the nearest one. A small selection is easier and more satisfying.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child faced with a long menu takes ages, picks something and then wishes he had picked another. More options make each seem less certain.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student compares dozens of colleges, phones or apps, stays unsure, and feels less satisfied with the final choice than if he had fewer options.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 23–26

rows.description: A wise decider sets criteria first, keeps a shortlist of three, and picks a good-enough option rather than searching for the perfect one.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22

rows.description: A teenager avoids asking someone out or applying for a competition, fearing the regret of failing more than the regret of never trying.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult picks the safe stream or job so that no one can say he made a mistake. Anticipated regret narrows choices, though inaction brings its own regret later.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young professional keeps every door open and delays commitment, fearing he might regret the road not taken. The delay itself becomes a cost.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22
